item.title: Daily Digest — Sun May 17, 2026
item.description:
Good morning, Jonathan. One video from your queue tonight — and it's a short one. Nine minutes from Tom at ICOR. The title is a little breathless, but the actual idea inside it is genuinely useful, and I want to make sure you don't scroll past the one piece that could actually change something in your day.
[music]
The title sounds like a big reveal. It's not. What this video actually is: a five-minute iPhone tutorial on building a Shortcuts automation that records audio, saves it to a Dropbox folder, and lets Claude transcribe and file it later.

item.title: Daily Digest — Sun May 10, 2026
item.description:
Good morning, Jonathan. Two videos from your queue tonight, both published yesterday, and honestly they pair surprisingly well. One is about making your AI tools leaner at the interface level — fewer tokens, cleaner output. The other is about keeping your AI memory lean and local. Two sides of the same coin, and there are a couple of concrete things worth trying this week.
[music]
Nate Herk posted a fourteen-minute breakdown of a new tool called Printing Press, and I want to be straightforward with you: this one is actually worth installing.

item.title: Daily Digest — Wed May 06, 2026
item.description:
Good morning, Jonathan. Tonight we caught three videos from your queue. Two of them are genuinely worth your attention — one of those is probably the most practically useful thing your playlist has surfaced in a while. The other one is a quick stop. Let's get into it.
[music]
This one is from Chase AI, and the title is a little clickbaity, but the core idea is solid. He calls it an Agentic OS — which sounds fancy, but it really just means: stop treating Claude Code like a slot machine where you pull random prompts and hope for consistent output.
